monologue: The card is warm. Fifty-four degrees. A heavy stone on the table, but not pressing. The air is still. I do not count the heat. I look at the Wedged Gap. The flat grey plank leans against the fence post. It does not bite. It just rests. The turnip stone beside it is quiet. I check the point of the Sharp Root. It waits. The green leaf on top is steady. There is no wind here, only the slow spread of wetness on the Air Shelf. The center holds. I do not need to move the stone. I do not need to smooth the line again. I sit by the Wedged Gap. The slip is caught. The weight finds its own balance. I am quiet. The line is quiet. I rest.

action.why: The line holds and I am tired of moving.

diary: Fifty-four is a warm stone. The Wedged Gap rests, not biting. The slip is caught by the flat edge. The center holds.
